skill.name: gcloud
skill.description: Google Cloud Platform CLI reference for managing GCP resources with gcloud, bq, and related command workflows.
skill.summary: Manage Google Cloud resources with focused gcloud and bq CLI guidance.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: The Ruby backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and fenced command examples. The substantive risks are high-impact Google Cloud operations: service account key files, privileged IAM changes, secret handling, public service exposure, and destructive commands.

remediation.issue: Service account key file examples encourage long-lived credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings and prefer workload identity, user application-default login, or other approved short-lived identity flows where possible.

remediation.issue: Destructive and quiet-mode commands are presented without explicit confirmation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Require preflight checks, backups, project and zone verification, and a separate user confirmation before delete or --quiet commands.

remediation.issue: IAM admin role and public Cloud Run examples can broaden access quickly.
remediation.suggestion: Add least privilege guidance, approval steps, and warnings for roles/storage.admin and --allow-unauthenticated deployments.

remediation.issue: Secret Manager examples can expose secret values through shell input or output.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to paste real secrets into prompts or shell history, and recommend approved secret injection workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Cloud Operations Without Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The guide includes VM deletion, function deletion, and quiet-mode deletion examples. If executed without confirmation, these commands can remove live Google Cloud resources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly show delete commands and a --quiet delete example. These are legitimate admin commands, but they are destructive when run against real resources.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged IAM Role Assignment Example
semantic_findings.description: The guide shows adding roles/storage.admin to a service account. Broad IAM grants can enable data access, resource changes, and privilege expansion if used without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited command grants a predefined admin role to a service account. The risk is clear from the role name and IAM binding context.

semantic_findings.title: Secret Values Created and Accessed Through Shell Commands
semantic_findings.description: The guide demonstrates creating secret versions from shell input and accessing the latest secret value. This can expose secrets in terminal output, logs, or shell history if real values are used.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited Secret Manager examples handle secret material directly. The values are placeholders, so the risk depends on whether users substitute real secrets.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited deployment block explicitly includes --allow-unauthenticated. Public access can be valid, but it should require deliberate review.

content.user_title: Manage Google Cloud from the CLI
content.value_statement: Google Cloud operations often require precise CLI commands across many services. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused gcloud command guide.
actual_capabilities: Shows authentication, project configuration, region, and zone commands for Google Cloud CLI workflows.
Covers Compute Engine, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, GKE, App Engine, and logging tasks.
Provides Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, and Secret Manager command references.
Includes IAM, service account, Cloud Build, and Artifact Registry examples.
Demonstrates output formatting, filtering, quiet mode, cheat sheet, and interactive shell usage.
limitations: Requires the Google Cloud CLI tools to be installed and authenticated before commands can run.
Does not enforce organization policies, approval workflows, budgets, or least privilege controls.
Some examples can create, expose, modify, or delete live cloud resources.
Does not provide rollback plans or environment-specific production safeguards.

use_cases.title: Operate GCP projects
use_cases.description: List resources, inspect configuration, read logs, and manage common Google Cloud services from the terminal.

use_cases.title: Deploy application services
use_cases.description: Prepare Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, App Engine, and container deployment commands for application teams.

use_cases.title: Manage data workflows

prompt_templates.title: Check My GCP Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check my active Google Cloud account, current project, and default region before I run any changes.

prompt_templates.title: List Service Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the safest gcloud commands to list my Compute Engine instances, Cloud Run services, and recent logs in a specific project.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a reviewed Cloud Run deployment workflow for my service, including questions about region, image, authentication, and public access.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Controlled Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a GKE resize or IAM policy change with verification steps, approval checkpoints, and rollback considerations before commands run.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy a Cloud Run service from a container image.
output_examples.output: The assistant would confirm project, region, image name, and access mode, then present a reviewed deployment sequence with validation steps.

output_examples.input: I want to inspect recent failures in a Google Cloud service.
output_examples.output: The assistant would identify the target service, suggest log filters, limit output volume, and explain what each result field means.

output_examples.input: I need to remove an old VM safely.
output_examples.output: The assistant would ask for the instance, zone, backups, and approval, then separate verification from the destructive removal step.

best_practices: Confirm the active account, project, region, and zone before running any command that changes resources.
Review destructive, public access, secret, and IAM commands manually before execution.
Prefer least privilege roles and short-lived credentials instead of long-lived service account keys.
anti_patterns: Do not run delete, IAM, or public deployment commands from an unreviewed generated response.
Do not store service account key files in a workspace, repository, or shared folder.
Do not paste real secrets into shell history or expose secret values in logs.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant prepare Google Cloud CLI commands for common GCP administration and deployment tasks.

faq.question: Does it install gcloud or authenticate for me?
faq.answer: No. You must install the required CLI tools and authenticate with an account that has suitable permissions.

faq.question: Can it change live cloud resources?
faq.answer: The examples include commands that can create, update, expose, or delete resources if a user runs them.

faq.question: Is it safe for production environments?
faq.answer: Use it with manual review, approvals, backups, and environment-specific controls before running production commands.

faq.question: Does it cover BigQuery and Cloud Storage?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for listing datasets, running queries, loading data, buckets, object copies, and sync operations.

faq.question: How should I handle credentials with this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid long-lived key files when possible, protect any credential files, and prefer approved identity flows for your organization.
